title: Exactly five perfect solids exist; Euclid ends there
body: For a convex solid of identical regular faces, angle arithmetic at each corner permits only the tetrahedron, cube, octahedron, dodecahedron and icosahedron to close. Euclid's Elements builds toward constructing all five and proving the list complete in the final book. Twenty-three centuries later the proof strategy is unchanged: count the angles, exhaust the world.
